## Summary of Results

The 2025 Australian federal election, held on May 3, resulted in a historic landslide victory for the Australian Labor Party, with Labor securing 94 seats in the House of Representatives. 

This represents the largest number of seats won by Labor at the federal level in its history. The Labor government, led by Anthony Albanese, was reelected with an increased 18-seat majority.

In comparison, the Coalition won 43 seats, while Greens, Centre Alliance, Katter's Australian Party each won 1 seat, and Independents won 10 seats.

## Summary of Australia's May 2025 Election Results

On May 3, 2025, Australia held its 48th federal election. The Labor Party, led by Anthony Albanese, secured a second consecutive term, winning 94 of 150 seats in the House of Representatives, with the opposition Liberal-National Coalition securing 43 seats.

**Key Results:**
- Labor garnered 34.8% of the primary vote and 54.9% of the two-party-preferred vote
- Anthony Albanese secured a second term as Prime Minister, while Opposition leader Peter Dutton conceded defeat in his Queensland seat of Dickson, becoming the first federal opposition leader in history to lose his own electorate
- Voter turnout stood at 90.7 per cent, a slight increase from 89.7 per cent in the previous 2022 election
- Approximately 69 (49.1 per cent) women will be elected to parliament, an increase from 58 (38 per cent) women elected to the 47th Parliament

This was characterized as a historic landslide victory for Labor, with significant losses for the Coalition across major cities.
